title: Finite modules over a regular local ring have finite projective dimension
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], and let $M$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Assume the module universe contains a small copy of $R$. Then there is $n\in\mathbf N$ such that $M$ has projective dimension at most $n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. This records the existing Ext-based source-library theorem; no dimension bound is needed.

proof.text: Use the existing proved source theorem IsRegularLocalRing.exists_hasProjectiveDimensionLE. Its preceding theorem proves finite projective dimension for R/p by noetherian induction on prime ideals: at the maximal ideal a regular sequence computes the residue-field projective dimension; otherwise choose y in m outside p, pass to the regular-element quotient, and use a prime filtration with strictly larger primes. The source theorem then applies prime-filtration induction to M, with annihilator lower bound zero. The zero module has projective dimension at most zero. The universe condition is exactly the source Small instance.
